name: Auschwitz-Birkenau
tagline: The former Nazi German concentration and extermination camp, preserved as a memorial and museum to the victims of the Holocaust.
highlight: Standing at the gate of Birkenau, a place that asks visitors to remember and reflect.
shortDescription: The Auschwitz-Birkenau Memorial and Museum, a UNESCO World Heritage Site near Kraków, where over a million people, most of them Jews, were murdered between 1940 and 1945.
metaDescription: An Auschwitz-Birkenau visitor guide: history, how to book tickets and guided tours, what to see at Auschwitz I and Birkenau, rules and etiquette, how to get there from Kraków and a half-day plan.
nearestAirport: Kraków John Paul II (KRK), about 1.5 hours by road
budget: US$30–80 for a guided visit, plus transport

image.alt: The gatehouse of Auschwitz II-Birkenau with railway tracks entering

intro: Auschwitz-Birkenau was the largest of the Nazi German concentration and extermination camps. Established in 1940 by Germany in occupied Poland, near the town of Oświęcim, it became the main site of the Holocaust: about 1.1 million people were murdered here, roughly one million of them Jews from across Europe, along with Polish prisoners, Roma and Sinti, Soviet prisoners of war and others. The camp was liberated by the Red Army on 27 January 1945.

Today the site is the Auschwitz-Birkenau State Museum, a memorial and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It has two main parts: Auschwitz I, the original camp of brick barracks, with exhibitions in preserved blocks and the gate with the words 'Arbeit macht frei', and Birkenau, 3 km away, a vast site with railway tracks, ruined gas chambers and rows of surviving barracks. Visitors come to bear witness, and to learn.

A visit is emotionally demanding, and it deserves preparation. Entry is by timed ticket and usually with a guided tour, which lasts about 3.5 hours, and it is not suitable for children under 14. It is best treated as a memorial rather than an attraction, with quiet, respect and time afterwards to reflect.

whyVisit.intro: A visit is not enjoyable, but many people find it one of the most important things they do in Europe.

points.title: Bearing witness
points.text: To the scale of the Holocaust.

attractionsIntro: The memorial has two sites, linked by a shuttle bus.

attractions.name: Auschwitz I

image.file: File:The arbeit macht frei gate in Auschwitz I.jpg
image.alt: The gate of Auschwitz I with its iron sign above the entrance

attractions.text: The original camp, with brick barracks that now house exhibitions on the history of the camp, the victims and the perpetrators, including personal belongings.

attractions.name: Auschwitz II-Birkenau

image.file: File:Auschwitz II German concentration camp selection ramp 2016 P11.jpg
image.alt: The selection ramp at Birkenau with railway tracks

attractions.text: The vast extermination camp, with the railway ramp, ruins of the gas chambers, the memorial monument and surviving barracks.
attractions.tip: Wear comfortable shoes and bring water.

attractions.name: The exhibitions
attractions.text: Permanent exhibitions in blocks, including national exhibitions and the display of victims' belongings.
attractions.tip: Photography is limited in some blocks.

attractions.name: The International Monument
attractions.text: A memorial at Birkenau with plaques in the languages of the victims.

attractions.name: The Auschwitz Jewish Center
attractions.text: A museum and synagogue in the town of Oświęcim.

attractions.name: Oświęcim town
attractions.text: The town outside the camp, with a Jewish history before the war.

thingsToDoIntro: A visit is a serious experience.

thingsToDo.title: Book a guided tour
thingsToDo.text: Educators lead groups through both sites.

thingsToDo.title: Read beforehand
thingsToDo.text: Survivor testimonies such as Primo Levi.

foodIntro: There is a cafeteria at the museum, but most visitors eat in Kraków.

gettingThere.intro: Auschwitz is about 65 km west of Kraków.

options.text: Coach transfers and guides from Kraków, about 6 to 8 hours in total.
Regular buses from Kraków take about 1.5 hours.
From Kraków to Oświęcim, then a local bus.

gettingAround.intro: A shuttle links the two sites.

bestTime.headline: April–May and September–October
bestTime.summary: The site is open all year, and the atmosphere is heavy whatever the weather.

seasons.text: Cold and quiet, and the atmosphere is stark.

bestTime.avoid: Peak July and August, and 27 January, the anniversary of liberation, when there are ceremonies.

days.title: Auschwitz-Birkenau
days.morning: Transfer from Kraków and tour Auschwitz I.

tipsIntro: A few tips help you prepare.
tips: Book tickets weeks ahead, directly from the museum.
Bring ID, and expect security checks.
Do not pose for selfies or treat it as a photo opportunity.

faq.q: How long does a visit take?
faq.a: About 3.5 hours for a guided tour.

faq.q: Can I visit without a guide?
faq.a: Yes at certain times, but book a slot online.
Entry without a guide is free at certain hours, though a ticket is still needed. Guided tours cost money.
It is not recommended for those under 14.
Yes in most places, but not in some rooms. Be respectful.
